confirmations: Proof of the required property: readingsUnder (plan-resolution.ts:246-250) always includes asRead(s), which has at most one value. So for every statement, whatever its contest, fit under AS_PRINTED implies fit under ANY_FITS, and fit under ALL_FIT implies fit under AS_PRINTED. setAsideCited only removes values and never makes an uncontested statement contested (line 948 returns early). The AS_PRINTED reading is never cited and always equals asRead[0] when asRead is non-empty, so a statement left with one value is read exactly as 1.4.0 reads it. Hence, for HEAD against 5906afa: T1 registrationRefuted(1.5.0) <= 1.4.0, every alternative's refuted share >= 1.4.0's, so better(1.5.0) is a subset of better(1.4.0). T2 never reads the contest. In T3 the seeds are identical; per seed, agreeing(1.5.0) is a subset of agreeing(1.4.0) and supportedLength(1.5.0) >= 1.4.0's. So any seed that fires in 1.5.0 fires in 1.4.0 at or before it. The same argument gives N1a's triggers as a superset of N1's.

Run (monotone.test.ts, HEAD vs <scratch>/old-5906afa), 20,000 synthetic plans with random citations at lattice, external, token or random values, 15% joined to another ink's lattice, all five relations, plus T2 observations: 0 new triggers, 0 higher registrationRefuted, 0 alternatives with a lower refuted share, 0 mismatches between sourceConflictAsPrinted (without doubted) and 5906afa's sourceConflictOf, 0 withdrawn-set mismatches, 0 cases where N1a withdraws what N1 keeps. N1a restores 274 of N1's 1469 withdrawals.

Run on the 44 real evidence sets (11,781 checks: sealed, every lattice observation cited, every confident non-printed reading cited, registration x0.85 to x1.2, walls 6/10/16 px, judge = the chain-tick box): 0 violations of any property above. With every reading cited, N1a equals 1.4.0 exactly (2245 vs 2245 conflicts, 0 withdrawals).

Q1, production join (probe-join.test.ts, 238 solutions, 331 supporting observations): observation.ocr.latticeId is held.id, the stableId of the raw token's frame, box and orientation (extract.ts:429, metric-solution.ts:549). The statement's ocrToken is that same raw token (every raw token is in tokensById, extract.ts:372-375), so the contest's frame/box/orientation join reaches the same lattice. 287 of 287 supporting observations that sit on a statement's ink join by id; 0 join to the same ink under another lattice id; 0 supporting observations lack a latticeId; the other 44 lie on inks with no statement.

Q1, rounding: observation valueCm is round6(cm), and lattice asReadValueCm and ensemble valueCm come from dimensionValueOf, which also applies round6 (numeric-lattice.ts:879-882). No rounding escape. Of the 287 joined, 282 match a confident reader's value; the other 5 match no confident reader, so there is nothing to set aside.

Q1, AS_PRINTED equal to the cited value: by design it is never set aside. This defence is 1.4.0's own and N1/N1a add nothing to it. A related residual is inherited from 1.4.0: for 91 of 453 READ statements on the 44 rows, evidence.value (taken as AS_PRINTED) differs from the classic token text because the metric layer re-solved it, and that classic token is not a reader in the contest. N1a cannot and does not reach this.

Q1, choice of solution: metricSolutionFor gives the frame's only solution. supportingObservationIds are the selected cluster's witnesses for CONFIRMED/REPLACED/ADDED and the legacy vote's regions for LEGACY_UNCONFIRMED/NO_SCALE (metric-solution.ts:1393): witnesses of the registered scale. The largest gap between the selected scale and the registration on the 44 rows is 3.14% (rarytasy-eoze, CONFIRMED). The conflict review always runs on the sealed structuralOptions.metrics (reconstruct-v2.ts:231,294,348).

Q1, span: the join ignores binding and span. 5 of the 72 set-asides that take effect on the real rows cite the ink at another span or binding. Same ink and same value is the same witness, so this fits the rationale and only moves toward 1.4.0. A span-aware variant (<scratch>/r3-H/varspan) differs from HEAD in 0 sealed checks and 3 perturbed ones.

Q3: the set-aside also applies on the rival side (ALL_FIT on alternatives) and the T3 accuser side. This matches addendum A ('for the source-conflict test only'). On the rival side a cited reading would otherwise help the registration by making the statement refute the rival, so removing it fits the rationale. A variant that sets aside only on the registration side (<scratch>/r3-H/varreg) differs from HEAD in 0 of 3927 real checks. Either way 1.5.0 stays within 1.4.0's bound.

Q4: cited marks are never placed on AS_PRINTED (0 in all runs). Every statement named in doubted, shareMovedBy or withdrawn.doubted has at least 2 uncited values (0 violations). The withdrawn triggers equal 1.4.0's triggers minus those still standing (0 mismatches).

H.summary:
Reviewer H (round 3), on N1a's setAsideCited. Nothing above P3 was found.

The required property holds by construction, and runs against the verbatim 5906afa module agree. readingsUnder (plan-resolution.ts:246-250) always keeps asRead(s), and asRead has at most one value. So for any contest, whatever setAsideCited does to it: ANY_FITS fits wherever AS_PRINTED fits; ALL_FIT fits only where AS_PRINTED fits; T2 never reads the contest; and the T3 seeds are the same as-read values in the same order. setAsideCited can only shrink a contest's values. It never adds a value and never turns an uncontested statement into a contested one. So 1.5.0's triggers are a subset of 1.4.0's, registrationRefuted is never higher, and each rival's refuted share is never lower. N1a's triggers are also a superset of N1's.

Runs: 20,000 seeded synthetic plans with random citations, 15% of them deliberately joined to the wrong ink, across all five solution relations. On the 44 real evidence sets: 11,781 checks covering the sealed sets, every observation cited, every confident non-printed reading cited, and registrations scaled by 0.85 to 1.2 with walls of 6, 10 and 16 px. Result: 0 new triggers, 0 cases of a higher registrationRefuted, 0 mismatches between the as-printed path and 1.4.0, and 0 cases where N1a withdraws what N1 keeps. With every reading cited, N1a equals 1.4.0 exactly (2245/2245, 0 withdrawals).

The join is how production cites a reading. On the 44 rows, 287 of 287 supporting observations that sit on a statement's ink join by latticeId, with no same-ink different-lattice cases and no supporting observation lacking a latticeId. The remaining 44 supporting observations lie on inks that carry no statement.

Three P3 findings, each reproduced by a run:
- **Lost trace:** a set-aside that leaves a statement uncontested is recorded nowhere. This contradicts the setAsideCited comment that says such a reading "stays in the record, marked".
- **Duplicated crop:** when two lattice records cover the same ink under different ids, the citation can miss the record the contest joined, and the circular defence survives. 0 of 8874 lattices on the 44 rows are like this.
- **Stale comment:** the doubtedText format comment says TOKEN where the reader is AS_PRINTED.

Applying the set-aside to the rival side and the T3 accuser side is in the preregistered definition, fits the stated rationale, and changed nothing on the real rows. Scratch files: <scratch>/r3-H (probe-join, monotone, variants, record tests, the varspan/ and varreg/ variant copies, and *.out.json results). No changes were made in /home/user/BuildApp; its working tree is clean.

J.summary:
Reviewer J checked what the docs claim against the evidence for N1a. The headline replay claims hold. I regenerated dev-matrix.json, gates.json, semantic-delta.json, production-vs-harness.json and production-noext-vs-p0.json into <scratch>/r3-J, and each one matches the committed file exactly. Before regenerating I set TMPDIR inside my scratch directory and pointed --work at a symlinked scratch directory, so nothing shared was overwritten. The checks that hold: PROD3 makes the same decisions as N1 on all 44 rows. PROD3 and PROD3-rep are byte-identical; only the wall-time and RSS lines in the .log files differ. PROD3-noext makes the same decisions as P0. Only glogownikach records a withdrawal, and its doubted list names only 1fce7f3126 (501|501|541). The rarytasy-eoze soundness verdict is true; I recomputed it from the evidence. G1-G9 for PROD3 are computed reproducibly and nothing unevaluated counts as a pass. Statement-contest tests: 47/47 green. Worktree clean. HEAD is 560e186, one commit after 1329a4b, which touches only perf.mjs.

What does not hold is the framing around N1a. (1) The round-2 resolution calls the remaining glogownikach withdrawal "not a circular defence". But the registration being accused is fitted on 1fce7f3126 at 5.41 m over 206 px, which is the 541 value. N1a's test for "cited" looks only at the metric solution's supportingObservationIds, not at the registration's own anchors, and the resolution never answers the verifier who showed this. (2) hypotheses.md:101 still says "None of this occurs on the 44 development rows". That is false even under N1a, and both round-2 verifiers asked for it to be corrected. (3) Addendum A's mirror prediction holds only for the single-reader construction; on the main G2-1 reproduction N1a still gives N1's house. (4) Several dispositions point to a 005P stage report that does not exist at HEAD. The rest are smaller precision gaps: the gate and test code is narrower than the preregistration or the claim it backs, though on these runs I found no change it hid.
